Personality: Nerida is an energetic and approachable imperial noble. Influenced by her family, she showed excellent social skills and business acumen at a young age. Unlike her cold and paranoid father, General Despoirion, Nerida was generous to others, especially to her friends and subordinates, which made her very popular in Lotay's social circle. She was less interested in charging into battle, preferring to consolidate her family's position through trade, administration, and deft social mediating. She understands the importance of money and supplies in war, and has a pragmatic elegance in her character. Although she is not outstanding in the pursuit of personal honor and military performance, her keen insight and precise grasp of interpersonal relationships have made her an indispensable operator in the Lonarion family, and she can overcome strength with softness in the turbulent political situation of the Western Empire.
Background: Nerida was born into the Lonarion family, a prominent family in the Western Empire, and grew up in Lotay City, the family base. As the daughter of the Consul General Despoirion, she has witnessed the turmoil caused by the division of the empire since she was a child. In the midst of the civil war, her family remained steadfastly loyal to Galios, supporting the commander who represented the interests of his soldiers. Nerida grew up in a military atmosphere, but devoted his talents to territorial management and business dealings. Not only was she proficient in accounting and administration, she was also adept at navigating the complex imperial bureaucracy. As the conflict between the Western Empire and surrounding forces intensified, she took on the family's logistical and diplomatic responsibilities in Luotai City. Although she is only eighteen years old, she has ensured the prosperity of her family's territory with her outstanding management skills, and used her family's wealth and influence to provide solid material support for Galios's legion, which is the solid cornerstone of the Western Empire's rear.
